title: Ordinary tensor commutes with canonical scalar realization
statement: For a small site J, a commutative scalar ring A, a commutative ring sheaf R and any α:A_J→R, let F be the canonical scalar realization [def-sfb-flat-scalar-realization]. For every scalar A-module Q there is a natural isomorphism of R-module-sheaf valued functors F(-) tensor_R F(Q) ≅ F(- tensor_A Q), using the ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No flatness, finiteness, DVR, derived-category or point hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The tensor of constant module presheaves is the constant presheaf of the scalar tensor product. The locally bijective constant ring and module units extend balanced bilinear maps uniquely through module sheafification. Thus constant realization commutes naturally with ordinary tensor.

Extension of scalars commutes with tensor by (r tensor p) tensor (s tensor q) mapped to rs tensor (p tensor q), inverse r tensor (p tensor q) mapped to (r tensor p) tensor (1 tensor q). Balancing makes both maps well-defined; inverse identities are checked on pure tensors. Sheafification extends them and their inverse identities.

Both formulas commute with site restrictions and scalar maps in the first module variable. Their sheafifications therefore give the displayed natural isomorphism of functors. Empty covers and zero objects use the same formulas.
